findings.title: Backup-code requests can bypass the password check by including a dummy TOTP value
findings.body: The password verification earlier in `authorize` runs only when `credentials.totpCode` is empty, while this new branch accepts a backup code whenever `credentials.backupCode` is set and does not validate the TOTP value. A caller can submit a valid backup code plus any non-empty `totpCode` value and an arbitrary or absent password; this skips password verification and the backup-code branch succeeds. The UI retains the password during the normal flow, but the credentials callback is directly callable. Require password verification independently of whether a TOTP field is present (or otherwise bind completion of the password step to the second-factor request) before accepting a backup code.

findings.title: Backup codes are consumed with a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The code list is read from the user record, checked in memory, and then written back after replacing the matched entry with `null`. Two concurrent login requests using the same code can both read the old encrypted list before either update occurs, both pass `indexOf`, and both create sessions; the last write merely overwrites the same resulting list. This violates the advertised one-time-use property. Consume the code atomically, for example by using a transaction/row lock or a conditional update that verifies the stored value has not changed and rejects the request when no row was updated.

findings.title: The new backup-code authentication and consumption behavior is not tested
findings.body: The added test coverage only verifies that the setup screen has downloadable/copyable controls; it does not submit a backup code through login or the disable-2FA flow, verify that a valid code succeeds, verify invalid-code handling, or verify that a used code cannot be reused. The test itself leaves these core feature paths as TODOs, so regressions in the newly added authentication branch and one-time-code behavior will not be caught.
